entries.title: Gut Microbiome in a Flowing Intestine Tube
entries.description: A transparent, gently peristalsing tube with flowing semi-transparent food particles where differently colored bacterial spheres attach to, detach from, and colonize the tube wall, form clusters, and are flushed along, with labels and a side bar graph showing population counts.

entries.title: Biofilm Growth on a Rock Surface
entries.description: A stationary rock slab on a light background where tiny bacteria spheres land from a flowing stream, attach, replicate into a layered biofilm sheet, excrete a faint translucent matrix that spreads, and occasionally detach as clumps that drift away.

entries.title: Soil Microbiome Around Plant Roots
entries.description: A central plant root cylinder extending through a semi-transparent soil box where nutrient particles slowly diffuse outward and diverse microbes move, attach to the root surface, form glowing nodules, and compete for nutrients shown as colored particle trails.
entries.seed: Soil Microbiome Around Plant Roots: A central plant root cylinder extending through a semi-transparent soil box where nutrient particles slowly diffuse outward and diverse microbes move, attach to the root surface, form glowing nodules, and compete for nutrients shown as colored particle trails.

entries.title: Microbes Competing in a Droplet
entries.description: A floating water droplet sphere in air filled with different colored motile microbes that randomly swim, collide, replicate, die, and form clusters, while the droplet slowly evaporates and shrinks, changing crowding and interaction rates.

entries.title: Oral Microbiome on Rotating Teeth
entries.description: A rotating jaw model with teeth where colored bacterial spheres land from incoming saliva droplets, colonize crevices, form sticky biofilms that thicken and become opaque, and are partially removed by a sweeping translucent toothbrush cylinder.

entries.title: Microbiome Succession After Antibiotics
entries.description: A rectangular chamber representing the gut lumen where initial diverse colored microbes move and replicate, then a transparent “antibiotic wave” sweeps through causing many to dissolve, followed by the regrowth and spatial expansion of a few surviving species with population meters.
entries.seed: Microbiome Succession After Antibiotics: A rectangular chamber representing the gut lumen where initial diverse colored microbes move and replicate, then a transparent “antibiotic wave” sweeps through causing many to dissolve, followed by the regrowth and spatial expansion of a few surviving species with population meters.

entries.title: Microbe–Phage Predator–Prey Dynamics
entries.description: A flat surface colonized by bacteria spheres where smaller glowing phage particles orbit and randomly collide with bacteria, attach, cause them to swell, then burst into multiple new phage particles that scatter, with live counters for host and predator numbers.
entries.seed: Microbe–Phage Predator–Prey Dynamics: A flat surface colonized by bacteria spheres where smaller glowing phage particles orbit and randomly collide with bacteria, attach, cause them to swell, then burst into multiple new phage particles that scatter, with live counters for host and predator numbers.

entries.title: Microbial Colony Expansion on a Petri Dish
entries.description: A top-down, slightly tilted Petri disk where single microbe seeds at the center replicate into growing colored circular colonies that expand, overlap, and change color at the edges, with faint radial trails marking expansion fronts over time.

entries.title: Microbiome Nutrient Gradient in a Chemostat

entries.title: Skin Microbiome on a Moving Hand
entries.description: A semi-transparent hand model with tiny microbes as colored dots that attach, detach, and move along the skin as the hand rotates, occasionally contacting a foreign surface that transfers some microbes, leaving faint colored “contact prints.”

entries.title: Microbes Forming a Symbiotic Network
entries.description: A lattice of plant roots and fungal filaments where microbial spheres attach to filaments, move along them like trains on tracks, transfer glowing nutrient particles between root nodes and microbes, and branch or retract filaments based on traffic.

entries.title: Microbiome as a Galaxy of Species Orbits
entries.description: A stylized “microbiome galaxy” where each species is a colored cluster of small spheres orbiting a central host sphere, with orbits expanding, contracting, and occasionally merging or splitting as “environmental events” pulses pass through.

entries.description: A flat, moist surface where motile bacteria start in a small central patch and swarm outward in coordinated moving bands, leaving behind ring-like high-density zones that slowly thicken or dissolve, with faint motion trails visualizing collective flow.

entries.title: Colonization of a New Sterile Surface
entries.description: A clean rectangular plate introduced into a chamber where airborne microbial particles drift, collide with the surface, sometimes stick, then replicate into patchy colonies that spread, merge, and change opacity as biomass accumulates.

entries.title: Microbiome Stability vs. Invasion
entries.description: A chamber filled with an established mix of microbes forming semi-stable colored clusters, then a new invading species cloud enters from one side, its particles attaching, displacing, or bouncing off residents depending on local density, with a stability “meter” bar.

entries.title: Microbes in a Turbulent Gut Mixing Vortex
entries.description: A curved, partially transparent intestinal loop where waves of peristalsis create swirling flows that tumble microbe particles and nutrient dots, concentrating them in eddies where microbes attach to walls, replicate, and then get stripped off by stronger vortices.

entries.description: A central crumb-like object slowly rotating in a fluid filled with microbes that attach to its surface, digest it by emitting transparent “enzyme clouds,” and cause the crumb to gradually shrink and pit, releasing nutrient particles that attract more microbes.

entries.title: Marine Microbiome Around a Sinking Particle
entries.description: A marine snow particle slowly sinking through a tall water column where free-living microbes swim and form dense halos around the particle, attach, release bubbles that alter its sinking speed, and detach as it breaks into multiple smaller particles.

entries.description: A rectangular chamber whose background color smoothly oscillates to represent pH, causing different microbial species to grow, shrink, or dissolve at different phases, with species blobs pulsating, splitting, or merging in sync with the pH wave.

entries.description: A 3D porous maze where two or three microbial types expand from different entrances, filling channels, colliding at junctions, and forming sharp colored boundaries that move as one species overgrows another under a gentle nutrient flow.

entries.description: A sequence of expanding translucent spheres representing host generations, each containing a cloud of microbes that replicate and drift in composition; at each “birth” event, a small sample of microbes transfers to a new sphere, which then grows and diverges in color mix.
